context: The scene takes place as O-lan, the matriarch of a wealthy family, lies dying. She is surrounded by her husband, Wang Lung, and her eldest son, who is about to marry the maid. O-lan is preoccupied with ensuring the continuation of her family line and expresses her wishes for their future, even as she prepares to die.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan informed Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening_third.speaker: Wang Lung
opening_third.text: Wang Lung rebuked O-lan, stating that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan explained to Wang Lung that she must die, as she felt it in her vitals, but would not die before her eldest son returned home and before he married the maid who was her daughter-in-law, and that she wanted him to ensure the maid served her well, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. She added that she wanted her son to come home and for him to marry the maid first, so that she may die easily, knowing his grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening_third.speaker: Wang Lung
opening_third.text: Wang Lung observed that O-lan looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan assured Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan remarked that the maid would be well, yet.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, as she wished to witness it all, and that it would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan inquired whether everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, and if they had put a full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan declared that she was content and that the thing in her may do as it will. She then instructed her son to look to his father and grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband, his father, his grandfather, and the poor fool in the court, adding that she had no duty to any other.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan conceded that even if she was ugly, she had borne a son, and that although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening_third.speaker: O-lan
opening_third.text: O-lan questioned how that one could feed him and care for him as she did, asserting that beauty would not bear a man sons.
